subject: orb weaver spider
title: A Spider Makes Its Captured Firefly Flash Like a Female

scenes.text: This spider catches one firefly, then uses it to catch more.
Male fireflies of one Asian species flash with two light organs. Females use only one.
When an orb weaver bites and wraps a male caught in its web, his signal changes.
He starts flashing with just one light, the way a female does.
Other males fly toward the fake female, and straight into the web.
Scientists think the venom causes it. The prisoner becomes the lure.

description:
In a 2024 Current Biology study in China, male Abscondita terminalis fireflies (which normally flash with two light organs, females with one) began flashing with a single organ after being bitten and wrapped by an orb-weaver spider, Araneus ventricosus.
Webs holding these captured males attracted more males than webs without a spider. The researchers suspect the venom causes the change.
Is the spider clever, or just lucky?
first_comment: The spider may not even know it's doing it. Clever trap or lucky venom?
